newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil seeks order amid police strike violence.
newsitem.headline: Brazil seeks order amid police strike violence.

text.p: The Brazilian authorities on Wednesday sought to restore order after a month-long police strike again ended in bloodshed.

A Justice Ministry spokeswoman said Justice Minister Iris Rezende had called on the states to punish mutinous civil and military police, who have taken to the streets, masked and armed, to demand better pay and conditions.

"Protesting with your gun in your hand is not a way to pressure the government over salaries. That's not pressure, that's aggression. It's gone beyond all limits," the spokeswoman quoted the minister as saying.

Two of the leaders of the police strike were arrested on Wednesday, and a special unit occupied the local division of the Association of Corporals And Soldiers of the Military Police, preventing protesters from meeting there.
"We are going to maintain security no matter the cost," said Ivandro Alves de Souza, civil police chief in Fortaleza.
"To strive for justifiable pay demands is okay. But it's not okay to set out on an armed struggle that threatens the safety of the population," Souza told Reuters in a telephone interview.
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso himself demanded action, presidency officials said.
"The lack of pay does not justify indiscipline," Cardoso said while visiting Sao Paulo on Tuesday.
Protests by police demanding salary increases have spread through more than a dozen of Brazil's 27 states since they began with bloodshed in the city of Belo Horizonte last month.

In Belo Horizonte, capital of Minas Gerais state, an officer died after being shot in a clash between striking civil police and on-duty military police, which despite their name are not part of the armed forces.
Two weeks ago, three people were injured when strikers traded shots with troops in the northeastern state of Alagoas.

And on Tuesday, up to five people were injured during a street battle between police protesters and a special military police unit in Fortaleza, capital of Ceara state, also in Brazil's poverty-stricken northeast.
Newspapers reported that three banks were robbed while civil and military police were trading shots on Tuesday in the centre of Fortaleza. Troops have been called out to maintain order.
